explanation: RAII is a fundamental C++ programming idiom that ties resource management to object lifetime.  It ensures resources (like memory, files, network connections, mutexes) are automatically acquired when an object is created and released when the object is destroyed, regardless of how the object's lifetime ends (normal execution, exception, etc.). This eliminates resource leaks and simplifies error handling.  Best practice involves using RAII consistently to avoid manual resource management, which is error-prone.
